regions.name: spine
regions.holds: VM, SU, sequencer, ports, tree top

regions.name: spine_port_tiles
regions.holds: result-port neighbourhoods: groups 0..95, the only ones whose fmul / VM write / argmax leaves can be active

regions.name: spine_scale_rom
regions.holds: 16 scale banks for each of the 96 port groups (RTL-compatible whole-image replica)

regions.name: spine_vm
regions.holds: 8 skew banks x 4 slices x 3 rows of 512x128 (VM_ELEMS 177,808 FP32) + steering

regions.name: spine_embedding_rom
regions.holds: INT8 embedding half-vocabulary + row scales

regions.name: spine_constants_sequencer
regions.holds: constant ROM, program, sequencer, ot_rom_tp_seq

regions.name: spine_stream_unit
regions.holds: reservation: SW = 1,024 stream unit at the ledger 12.8 mm2 (RTL is SW = 1)

regions.name: spine_tree_top
regions.holds: split-tree levels 9..13 registers and result compaction toward the port tiles

connections.name: x operand: VM -> farthest group (mq_x)
connections.note: ot_hdc_matvec: VM read returns at c+1 and mq_x captures at c+2, one cycle from the VM macro to every group. Priced one way, which needs the VM to stream x (it knows the address sequence) rather than tiles requesting it (a round trip, twice this). S distinct elements a cycle (<= 2048) multicast to G/S groups; exposed once per matrix op

connections.name: issue broadcast: sequencer -> farthest tile (instruction, go)
connections.note: same path and direction as the x stream, so it overlaps it (not added twice); the die RTL is one ot_hdc_matvec whose single issue register drives every group

connections.name: split tree + result compaction: farthest tile -> port tile (gate/up, S = 64)
connections.note: per-level partner distances on the placed grid; an adding level gives one register cycle of wire, a holding level TA+1 = 4 (u_hold + lq)

connections.name: split tree + result compaction: farthest tile -> port tile (o, down, S = 2048)
connections.note: as above

connections.name: split tree + result compaction: farthest tile -> port tile (qkv, S = 256)
connections.note: as above

connections.name: split tree + result compaction (lm_head, S = 1024)
connections.note: as above

connections.name: result write: port tile -> VM
connections.note: the matvec output registers o_*1 and o_*

connections.name: KV operand: tile KV slice -> mq_kv
connections.note: the ring slice sits in the tile (the KV operand of all 6,144 groups is 3.1 Mbit a cycle and cannot cross the die); needs FP8 packing and a per-group KV port (gap G8)

connections.name: KV fill: HBM service band -> farthest tile slice
connections.note: prefetch one layer ahead (ot_hdc_kv_stream discipline): bandwidth-, not latency-bound

connections.name: TP exchange: port tiles -> UCIe PHY and back
connections.note: ot_rom_oneshot_allreduce LAT 11 models the link hop only; the crossing from the spine to the west-edge PHY and back is not in the RTL

bisection.note: demand counts every priced stream once at full width (an upper bound); the centralised-KV line shows why the ring slice must live in the tiles
